Kimberly,

Thanks for sending this over. We reviewed Exhibit B and sketched a redline (attached) that keeps the concept simple for our finance team: if actual monthly usage for any calendar quarter drops by more than 15% compared to the prior quarter, Acme is eligible for a bandfall credit equal to the prorated difference between invoiced and actual usage, up to 100% of the invoiced delta for that quarter.

Key asks from our side:
- The trigger should be applied per calendar quarter (we do not want lookbacks longer than one quarter).
- Credits should flow automatically against the following invoice; no separate true-up invoice cycles.
- No grandfathered caps — our position is that contractual protection covers both parties and limiting credits creates revenue volatility for Acme.

Attached: ACME_redline_orderform.docx (redline), commentary.pdf (one-page rationale).

Please confirm you received and whether Redwood can accept the automatic invoice offset approach.

Kim / Karthik — quick internal notes after reading Acme's redline:

1) Trigger mechanics:
- Instead of a pure >15% drop from prior quarter, propose a dual threshold: (a) >12% drop AND (b) absolute delta >= 10,000,000 tokens in the quarter. That avoids micro-credit churn for small customers.

2) True-up cadence and offset:
- We can accept automatic invoice offsets but with two guardrails: (i) cap on applied credits per quarter at 50% of that quarter's invoice; (ii) right to request a reconciliation notice (30 days) if the usage metric appears inconsistent. This keeps offsets operationally simple but bounded.

3) Annual aggregate cap:
- Recommend an annual aggregate cap (12-month rolling window) equal to 200% of the highest single-credit quarter in the prior year. Gives Acme relief while limiting cumulative exposure.

4) Auditability:
- Add a short clause referencing the metrics feed (token-metering agreement + URL) and an audit process (1x/year, 30-day notice) to resolve disputes around measurement.

5) Draft language: I've annotated the attached consolidated redline with bracketed suggestions (see redline_consolidated.docx).

If we agree, I'll feed this to Legal (Irene) to convert into precise contract language. I also attached a sample bandfall-matrix (bandfall-matrix.csv) showing how credits would apply across sample usage profiles.

-M

Subject: Re: Order form: volume bandfall procedure - consolidated redline for review

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing Acme's rationale. We've consolidated and tried to balance Acme's operational preference for automatic offsets with Redwood's need to limit open-ended liability. Highlights of the redline we are sending:

- Trigger: bandfall applies when (A) quarter-over-quarter usage drops by more than 12% AND (B) the absolute reduction for the quarter is at least 10,000,000 tokens.
- Offset mechanics: credits may be automatically applied to the next invoice, subject to a quarterly cap of 50% of that invoice.
- Annual cap: 12-month rolling aggregate cap equal to 200% of the highest single-credit quarter in the prior 12 months.
- Audit and metric feed: credits are calculated from the token-metering feed (linked in Exhibit C). Either party may request an audit once per year with 30 days' notice.

We've attached the consolidated redline (redline_consolidated.docx) and a toy matrix (bandfall-matrix.csv) showing three scenarios. Legal (Irene) has flagged a couple of precise phrasing edits in the redline; if Acme agrees to the capped-offset approach we can translate those into final contract language and move to signature.

Please review by EOD Friday and let me know if Acme accepts the capped-offset model or if you need the uncapped language for internal approvals. If you accept, we'll have legal ship an updated signature-ready order form.

Best,
Kim
